title: Bihu Dance
description: The traditional folk dance of Assam performed during Rongali Bihu, marking the Assamese New Year and the onset of spring. Dancers in traditional Mekhela Sador perform graceful movements.

title: Bamboo Flute
description: The bamboo flute (bansuri) is a cherished musical instrument across Northeast India, especially among the Assamese and Manipuri communities.

title: Muga Silk
description: The golden Muga silk of Assam is unique to the Brahmaputra valley. It has a natural golden sheen and becomes softer with every wash.

title: Shillong Cherry Blossom
description: Shillong hosts India's only cherry blossom festival every November, transforming the hill station into a pink wonderland.

title: Assamese Thali
description: A complete Assamese meal served on a bell metal plate with rice, dal, fish curry, khar, pitika, and seasonal vegetables.

title: War Dance of Nagaland
description: The energetic warrior dance performed by Naga tribes during Hornbill Festival, showcasing bravery and tribal unity.

title: Muga Silk Weaving
description: The ancient art of handloom weaving Muga silk in Assam, passed down through generations of weavers in rural households.

title: Rongali Bihu
description: The most important festival of Assam celebrating the Assamese New Year with traditional songs, dances, feasts and community gatherings.

title: Manipur Pena Dance
description: A classical dance form of Manipur performed with a traditional string instrument called Pena, often depicting Radha-Krishna stories.

title: Naga Shawl
description: Handwoven shawls with distinctive geometric patterns that represent each Naga tribe's identity and social status.

title: Meghalaya Living Root Bridge
description: The famous living root bridges of Meghalaya, grown from rubber tree roots by the Khasi and Jaintia tribes over centuries.

title: Assamese Xorai
description: A traditional Assamese offering tray made of bell metal, used to offer betel nut and pan to guests as a mark of respect.

title: Manipur Raas Leela
description: The divine dance-drama of Manipur depicting the childhood antics of Lord Krishna, performed during Kartik Purnima.

title: Mizo Cheraw Dance
description: The bamboo dance of Mizoram where dancers step in and out of rhythmic bamboo poles, requiring great skill and coordination.

title: Tripura Garia Dance
description: A traditional dance of Tripura performed during the Garia festival, celebrating the deity of wealth and prosperity.

title: Sikkimese Prayer Flags
description: Colorful prayer flags strung across Sikkimese monasteries, carrying mantras on the wind to spread peace and compassion.

title: Arunachal Monpa Dance
description: The traditional dance of the Monpa tribe in Arunachal Pradesh, performed during Losar and Torgya festivals.

title: Assamese Bihuwor Axali
description: The traditional early morning feast of Bihu where neighbors exchange traditional delicacies like pitha, laru and curd.

title: Khasi Betel Leaf
description: The betel leaf (kwai) holds deep cultural significance in Khasi society, offered during ceremonies and daily conversations.

title: Naga Kheisa
description: Dried meat preparation traditional to Naga tribes, smoked over wood fire for preservation, a staple in Naga households.

title: Assamese Jaapi
description: The traditional conical hat of Assam made from bamboo and palm leaves, a symbol of Assamese identity and agrarian life.

title: Mizoram Pawl Kut Festival
description: The harvest festival of Mizoram celebrating the end of the jhum cultivation season with feasting, dancing and merriment.

title: Assamese Kolha Nritya
description: A tribal dance form of the Tea Garden community in Assam, performed during harvesting and festival seasons.

title: Manipuri Ema Market
description: The world's largest all-women market in Imphal, Manipur, where women trade everything from vegetables to handloom.

title: Tripura Unakoti Carvings
description: Ancient rock-cut sculptures dating back to 7th-9th century in Tripura, depicting Hindu deities in magnificent size.

title: Sikkimese Butter Tea
description: Traditional Tibetan-style butter tea made with yak butter and salt, a warming drink in the cold Sikkimese climate.

title: Arunachal Tawang Monastery
description: The largest Buddhist monastery in India located in Tawang, Arunachal Pradesh, founded in the 17th century.

title: Assamese Bhupen Hazarika songs
description: The immortal songs of Dr. Bhupen Hazarika, the cultural icon of Assam whose music transcends borders.

title: Khasi Nongkrem Dance
description: A sacred thanksgiving dance performed by Khasi women during the Nongkrem festival to honor Ka Blei Synshar.

title: Naga Morung System
description: The traditional community dormitory system of Naga tribes where young men learn warfare, culture and community values.

title: Mizo Solikhia Tradition
description: The traditional Mizo practice of courtship through music and poetry, where young men sing outside a girl's house.

title: Assamese Tussar Silk
description: The wild silk of Assam with its natural dark texture, used to create beautiful Mekhela Sador and traditional garments.

title: Sikkimese Losar Festival
description: The Tibetan New Year celebrated in Sikkim with mask dances, butter sculptures and community prayers at monasteries.

title: Manipur Polo
description: Manipur is considered the birthplace of modern polo, with traditional Sagol Kangjei played for centuries.

title: Arunachal Nyokum Festival
description: The harvest festival of the Nyishi tribe in Arunachal Pradesh, invoking the deity Nyokum for prosperity and well-being.

title: Tripura Kok Borok Language
description: The native Tripuri language spoken by the Tripuri people, rich in oral literature and folk traditions.

title: Assamese Jaapi Making
description: The traditional craft of making Jaapi from bamboo strips and Tokou palm leaves, requiring skilled craftsmanship.

title: Cherrapunji Rainfall
description: Known as one of the wettest places on Earth, Cherrapunji's monsoon rains shape the culture and architecture of Khasi hills.

title: Mizo Chai Ceremony
description: The traditional Mizo tea ceremony where families gather to share tea and stories, strengthening community bonds.

title: Naga Angami Sekrenyi
description: The purification festival of the Angami Nagas, marking the end of the agricultural year with rituals and feasting.
